scope: WRA01-WRA05: 5 models, 38 named canonical cases, 44 separately exposed named subfixtures
publication: No commit or push authorized or performed by this slice

independentInputs.authorship: WP0 source-only profile inputs and literal expected facts were written before production remote evaluator. No expected answers were generated from evaluator outputs. This is authorship independence, not OS-enforced isolation.
independentInputs.stepSequenceInterpretation: Independent manifest stepSequence names the ordered explanation checkpoints. Execution stops at the declared first detector for rejected proof/admission/applicability, or at the denied resource; prohibitedDownstreamEffects and expected firstDetector specify the truncated path. It does not assert later checkpoints execute after a terminal rejection.

exports.WINDOWSREMOTELAB_ATTRIBUTES: Cheap frozen static union field metadata; wra_01_ through wra_05_ namespaces
exports.WINDOWSREMOTELAB_SOURCES: Primary source references; exact byte/revision/hash/claim records in sources-remote.json
exports.WINDOWSREMOTELAB_SCENARIOS: 5 lazy model descriptors lab-wra01 through lab-wra05; no all-case construction at import
exports.buildWindowsRemoteSmbReference: (inputOverrides={}) -> raw SMB-shaped local/domain reference for source composition. Noncanonical helper does not add a catalog case. TARGET + Kerberos and EnableLUA0 explicitly reject.
exports.evaluateWindowsRemoteContext: Pure account/policy-to-source-owned authorization context operation, never keyed by case ID
exports.evaluateWindowsRemoteAccess: Pure requested-mask and ordered allow/deny ACE evaluation; enabled and deny-only SID attributes are decision inputs
exports.buildSmbAccessReference: Narrow opt-in carrier export in smb-access-lab.js; existing presets omit remote and retain default identities/mechanisms/decisions

modelAPI.defaultVariantId: First canonical short case ID. withVariant('default') aliases it; default is not an additional selectable case
modelAPI.withVariant: Builds only the selected case, rejects unknown case IDs with RangeError
modelAPI.subfixtureChoices: Named members for the selected canonical case, not Boolean hidden comparisons
modelAPI.withSubfixture: Builds the named member within the current canonical case; unknown member rejects with RangeError
modelAPI.state: Canonical initialState.workstation plus step.protocolEffects; no alternate narrative state engine
modelAPI.inventory: workstationInventory {artifacts,initial,events,bindings,reuse}; sender preparation, receipt/unwrap/acceptance, response decisions and cleanup are source-owned
modelAPI.positions: Explicit compactPositions and expandedPositions for every used actor. Target SAM is a logical child role within target physical host
modelAPI.decisionBindings: Proof authority/result, admission, context mode, resource decision, transmission, receipt, client knowledge, first boundary, retained prior session and preserved source desktop

tokenComparisonState.path: workstation.tokenComparison; null until the post-admission target-token-comparison operation
tokenComparisonState.ownership: target-filter-input authorization-input artifact and token-comparison comparison artifact are created and retained only at smbServer after actual proof and target admission; neither is seeded or sent to the client
tokenComparisonState.before: Modeled target-side filter input/reference with usableToken=false, no tokenId, target owner/account/userSid, enabled input group attributes and present-enabled or present-disabled privilege reference rows; not a source-client token or observed native full token
tokenComparisonState.after: Applied actual target-context artifactRef, owner/account/userSid/type/mode, group attributes and privilege inventory; no extra token or grant is created
tokenComparisonState.privileges: Rows {name,before:{present,enabled,state},after:{present,enabled,state}}; state is enabled, disabled or removed, with enabled=null when absent
tokenComparisonState.policy: Comparison retains appliedPolicy and policyRef at context creation; separate workstation.configuredPolicy follows later configuration changes while workstation.appliedPolicy remains the original context snapshot
tokenComparisonState.readablePolicy: workstation.policyComparison has label, policyLabel, registryValueName, registryPath, polarity, configured and applied records; records expose rawLATFP, effectiveLATFP, latfpDisplay, applyRemoteRestrictions, restrictionsDisplay, EnableLUA, FilterAdministratorToken and administratorProtection; applied remains null before accepted context
tokenComparisonState.verdict: workstation.verdictExplanation starts null, is set by the first actual proof/admission/resource/applicability decision, and is retained; successful reads set it only at authenticated client acceptance, never from initial false flags
tokenComparisonState.bounds: Exact native integrity/elevation fields remain unknown; AP needs-evidence and unavailable profiles create no new tokenComparison or appliedPolicy
tokenComparisonState.learnerSources: Runtime source sections and support note now identify primary clauses and applicability qualifications, not worker/test manifest paths

localComparisonResults.scope: WRA05 unavailable-profile/nonadmin-listed and WRA04 management-endpoint-denied produce explicitly qualified local lesson outcomes, not operation wire responses
localComparisonResults.ownership: comparison-result and endpoint-local-result are created at smbClient by the local lesson; only smbClient reads/holds these local outputs. The modeled target endpoint-result remains target-owned and is never acquired by C
localComparisonResults.canonicalState: workstation.localComparisonKnown starts false and becomes true at the actual client-local computation that creates/holds the result; clientKnowsResult, returnedResult and local domain/qualification are set at that same checkpoint. Later learner inspection grants no knowledge.
localComparisonResults.compatibility: clientKnowsResult and returnedResult preserve the original case outcome labels; a WSMan.AccessDenied label here identifies a simulated target-rule outcome, not a received WSMan fault packet
localComparisonResults.wireFlags: Local comparisons never write responseTransmitted or responseReceived and never add transmit/receipt stages or result-message edges; real preceding authentication/session history is retained and actual protected SMB operation responses still use their separate wire flags and SMB/NTSTATUS resultDomain
localComparisonResults.stages: applicability-result -> applicability-accept or endpoint-result-local -> endpoint-result-accept, all client-local with no protocol layers
localComparisonResults.bindingLifecycle: localComparisonKnown is equivalent to the retained client-owned local result holding at every compiler checkpoint. Reused-session priorSession is bound to a retained reused-session-record created atomically with the configured-policy-change state; that record references the already-held original sessionContextRef and tokenRef and does not create another authenticated session.
localComparisonResults.immutableInputs: WP0 case/profile expectations and raw source snapshots remain unchanged; no expectation hashes were repinned

namedSubfixtures.otherCases: One default subfixture each; total 44 including all 38 canonical representatives

reuseSemantics.reused: Replay includes the original accepted logon/proof/key history under effective LATFP0, then a distinct configured-policy-change snapshot to LATFP1, then the operation on that same already-established session/context. No new authentication occurs after the policy change. Original token and key history remain inspectable.
reuseSemantics.fresh: Separate fresh logon applies LATFP1 and obtains its own full-reference context
reuseSemantics.later-proof-denial: A separately seeded previously accepted filtered session remains held while a later new proof attempt is rejected. New session and resource checks are prohibited; prior session is not erased

tests: Local SAM and domain NTLM really use distinct authorities and key paths
Domain nonjoined Kerberos has explicit prerequisites and independent ticket/subkey histories
Signed denial uses established SigningKey/AES-CMAC and separates result boundaries
Encrypted error uses S2C key and nonce, never C2S or SigningKey as encryption key
RID500 classification follows SID/RID, not display name, and native fields stay unknown
Reused session binds original policy while fresh comparison applies changed policy
Deny-only SID matches deny, never allow; masks and privilege presence are actual inputs

clauses: Network type3 differs from RemoteInteractive type10
DCOM, WMI namespace and object rights separate
sourceClauseStepTestMappings.scope: WinRM endpoint rule is a bounded local authorization comparison after accepted SSPI first-hop identity; SMB carries the reused proof/key reference, not invented WinRM packets. Canonical RDP remains a separate linked implementation. No WMI protocol expansion.

clauses: Exact broad policy and SID-list policy
tests: AP broad/list exceptions are target-admin qualified and unresolved cases do not fabricate denial

limits: No native Windows/DC access or captured token/event/packet observation. Source-only deterministic semantics do not establish native interoperability or blanket RFC conformance.
Precise integrity, elevation and native token inventory fields remain unknown, including RID500 FAT1/LATFP1. Supported source-qualified grant comparisons remain available.
AP overview availability and CSP Windows Insider Preview [11.0.26100.9278] remain visibly different. No Windows Server or universal modern-Windows default claim.
Listed AP nonadmin returns needs-evidence without membership grant or definite operation denial/elevation. Unsupported AP build returns unavailable-profile without classic fallback.
All cryptographic objects are accepted symbolic expressions and provenance histories, not computed production cryptographic bytes.
Inherited human G01, performance owner conditions and historical review limitations are unchanged
